de25_location.topic: Location data: bidstream, brokers sold to government, carriers, Hemisphere/DAS, court limits

claims.text: FTC proposed order 9 Jan 2024 against X-Mode/Outlogic: sold precise location tied to mobile advertising IDs, not anonymised; clients included private government contractors; no sensitive-location filtering until May 2023; vote 3-0

FTC technology blog 3 Dec 2024: ad auctions broadcast consumer data, sometimes including location, to dozens of bidders in milliseconds; Mobilewalla allegedly kept data from auctions it lost; 'location data is sensitive data, full stop'

FTC final order vs Gravy Analytics and Venntel, 14 Jan 2025, 5-0: bans sale/use of sensitive location data except in limited national security or law enforcement circumstances; complaint alleged collection without consent for commercial and government uses

CBP paid just under $476,000 for Venntel software on 5 Aug 2020; Venntel sells app-derived phone movements searchable by area or device ID; WSJ Feb 2020 reported agencies used it for border crossings and arrests; IRS-CI used Venntel for a year and located no targets (Wyden's office)

DHS OIG-23-61 (Sept 2023): CBP, ICE and Secret Service did not follow DHS privacy policy or obtain Privacy Impact Assessments required by the E-Government Act before buying commercial telemetry data; shared passwords, no supervisory review; a CBP employee used the data to track coworkers (reported 20 Aug 2020); recommended ICE stop using it until PIAs approved

404 Media 8 Jan 2026: ICE's Penlink Webloc can watch a neighbourhood for phones and follow devices over time, from data on hundreds of millions of phones; an internal ICE legal analysis said it can be queried without a warrant

70 members of Congress wrote to DHS IG Cuffari on 3 Mar 2026 asking for a probe of ICE location purchases incl. the no-bid Penlink contract with a Webloc licence; ICE cancelled a hearing appearance in Feb 2026

EFF/AP 1 Sep 2022: Fog Data Science sold police app-derived location histories, claiming billions of points on 250m+ devices, for under $10,000 a year; at least 18 agency clients; searches often without warrants

FBI Director Patel told the Senate on 18 Mar 2026 'We do purchase commercially available information that is consistent with the Constitution and the laws'; Wray had said in 2023 the FBI previously bought location data but was not currently doing so

FCC fined carriers in Apr 2024 for selling customer location to aggregators without consent: AT&T ~$57m, Verizon ~$46.9m, T-Mobile $80m, Sprint ~$12m (~$200m total); the Supreme Court upheld the AT&T and Verizon fines 8-1 on 4 Jun 2026 (Roberts; Thomas dissenting), rejecting the jury-trial challenge; Fifth Circuit had sided with AT&T, Second Circuit with FCC

Wyden letter 20 Nov 2023: Hemisphere (2009-13 name) / Data Analytical Services pays AT&T to search domestic call records back to 1987, ~4bn records added daily, 'trillions' of records; searches often by subpoena; ONDCP funding paused 2013, resumed 2017, paused 2021, $270k in 2022

Chatrie v. United States, 29 Jun 2026: Kagan for five, Gorsuch concurring in judgment, Alito, Thomas, Barrett dissenting; accessing Google Location History via geofence is a search; warrant's probable cause and particularity remanded; 150 m radius, one hour around a bank robbery; Google moved Location History on-device in 2023

Judge Carlton Reeves (S.D. Miss.), Aug 2026: tower-dump warrants are general warrants and per se unconstitutional; upheld magistrate's denials of requests for towers near nine crime scenes; 'The government cannot have access to an entire haystack because it may contain a needle'
